split.method: episode-family holdout; F.28 development scenarios retained; new deterministic holdout episodes

false_negative_analysis.single_point_miss_duration: Not specified by F.28; each is a single sampled point.
interpretation: Gradual CPU drift labels become positive before the configured 5.0 MAD threshold is crossed; this is threshold latency, not missing input.
Low request-rate steps remain below 5.0 MAD and low-direction request-rate deviations are not actionable; their positive labels express the benchmark's assumed anomaly definition.
Each miss pattern repeats once per service, so the four service copies are not independent scenario families.

holdout.purpose: Validate unchanged 5.0-threshold policy on deterministic episodes not used in F.28 development analysis.
assumptions: Injected synthetic episodes are labeled anomalous by construction.
Stable-center and bounded-noise controls are assumed normal.
Scenario families and all their points remain wholly in holdout.
The holdout is small and synthetic; results do not establish live accuracy.

decision.reason: No detector change is justified by assumed synthetic labels and repeated narrow scenario families; changing the threshold would require independently reviewed operational labels and false-positive acceptance criteria.
